The Prophet feared the world's splendour for his people: wealth is sweet and green, blessed when given to the poor, orphans and travellers, but taken wrongly it never satisfies.
The Prophet would not enter Fatima's house because of a decorated curtain, saying he had no interest in worldly things, and had it sent to needy people.

The Prophet fears only worldly blessings: wealth is sweet vegetation, excellent when lawfully gained and spent on Allah's cause, orphans, the poor and travellers; the unlawful taker is never satisfied.
As Abu Ubaida brings Bahrain's jizya, the Prophet tells the Ansar he fears not their poverty but luxury, over which they will compete and be destroyed like past nations.
After praying for Uhud's martyrs, the Prophet said he sees his Fount and holds the world's treasure keys, and fears not polytheism for them but rivalry for worldly things.
Many are cheated of health and free time; true life is the Hereafter's; live as a stranger; hope outruns one's term, while love of wealth and long life grows.
The Prophet feared not his people's poverty but worldly wealth pouring in and their competing for it; wealth is sweet, a good helper if earned lawfully and spent rightly.
Khabbab said companions who died took none of their reward in this world, while those after them gathered wealth they could spend only on building.
Whoever looks at someone given more property and better appearance should also look at someone below him.
When a bedouin's camel outran the Prophet's swift she-camel Al-Adba, he said Allah lowers whatever is raised high in this world.
After praying over Uhud's martyrs, the Prophet said he saw his Fount and held the keys to earth's treasures, fearing not their worshipping others but their rivalry over worldly treasures.
Abu Barza said Islam lifted the Arabs from misery, but worldly wealth brought mischief, and the factions in Sham, Mecca and among his hearers fought only for worldly gain.
